summary: Defined the minimum frontend-only architecture for OncoReady's deterministic reset-to-closure treatment-readiness journey using synthetic browser state and no live services.
decisions: Implement CORE-001 as one React + TypeScript + Vite browser application backed by typed synthetic fixtures and a deterministic reducer or equivalent state machine.
Use one workflow-event source of truth to derive the staff queue, Treatment Readiness Graph, timeline, patient status, and caregiver projection so demo surfaces cannot drift.

Keep routing and task transitions deterministic: one readiness submission creates separate clinical-review and transportation-navigation tasks, and treatment confirmation requires staff action plus patient acknowledgment.
Treat clinical text as preserved, untrusted input routed to human review; no AI or client heuristic may make a clinical decision or control workflow safety.
Enforce the caregiver demonstration boundary through an explicit local permission projection that excludes clinical concern and task details from Ana's view.
Use browser persistence with safe schema/version fallback and a universally available one-click reset to protect the primary demonstration journey.

Require Gemini Phase A because this task establishes the product's first design system and a new signature visible workflow; architecture specifies capabilities and constraints but no aesthetic treatment.
Do not create an API contract because there is no live external or independently implemented component boundary in this slice.

risks.description: Independently scripted screens could diverge and make the five-minute demonstration show contradictory ownership or completion state.
risks.mitigation: Derive every surface from one guarded workflow state and append-only event history, and cover the complete reset-to-confirmed path in the smoke check.

risks.description: A simulated clinical workflow or role switch could be mistaken for validated triage, production authorization, or a live Ochsner integration.
risks.mitigation: Use explicit synthetic/simulated disclosure, preserve original clinical text for named human review, and avoid production, compliance, or clinical-decision claims.

risks.description: Caregiver projection errors could expose Maria's synthetic clinical concern and undermine the intended data-minimization story.
risks.mitigation: Create the caregiver view from an allowlisted transportation permission projection and assert clinical-data exclusion in the critical-path smoke check.

risks.description: Stale or malformed browser persistence could break a deadline-critical live demonstration.
risks.mitigation: Version persisted state, fall back to the deterministic opening fixture on incompatibility, make reset available from every main surface, and rehearse the offline build.

notes_for_next_agent: Gemini must complete design Phase A and the design digest gate before production frontend coding because frontend_design_required=true.
Build the golden path and state model before static contextual cases or explanatory integration panels; only Maria's case needs full interactivity.
Internal TypeScript types are not a formal task contract. Do not invent endpoints or implement against the repository's empty OpenAPI placeholder.
Make reset, guarded transitions, caregiver clinical-data exclusion, reduced-motion equivalence, and truthful synthetic labeling demo-critical requirements.
SMOKE depth requires implementation-owned build and critical-path verification only; no independent tester or dedicated security reviewer is selected.
